implementation_summary: checkLinks now applies the crawl's own rules again to every link target before it can be requested: isCheckoutPath (always on, safe default with no policy), pathLimitVerdict (when the new optional pathLimits {includePaths, excludePaths, startPath} is passed) and RobotsPolicy.isAllowed(pathname+search) (when the new optional robots is passed). It reuses area-detect.ts, limits.ts and the RobotsPolicy type and copies none of them. A refused target is neither requested nor reported (even with a crawl status) and does not use up maxRequests. The result shape (AuditFinding[]) has no skipped count, so refused targets are not counted. content-problems.ts and seo-basics.ts make no requests and were left unchanged.

tests_executed.name: fail-before check (refusal check temporarily disabled, then restored)
tests_executed.output_excerpt: Tests 4 failed | 12 passed (16): the 4 new robots/checkout/limits/allowed tests fail without the fix

tests_proposed: Once wired: an analyse-site or pipeline integration test checking that a robots-disallowed link missing from coverage.skipped (crawl timed out) gets no request
risks: The robots and path-limit checks do nothing in production until they are wired: analyse-site.ts (not owned by BE-305 or BE-192) builds the checkLinks options and must pass robots and pathLimits through, and AuditCrawlResult in crawl.ts does not expose the RobotsPolicy yet. Only the checkout/payment refusal is active today.
Behaviour change: a broken link to a checkout/payment path is no longer reported, even with a crawl status. No other audit test depends on the old behaviour (checked by grep).
broken-links.ts now imports audit/crawl/area-detect.ts, which loads deterministic-spider.ts at runtime. There is no import cycle; tests load fine.
Contract: CheckLinksOptions only gained optional fields (robots, pathLimits) and LinkPathLimits is newly exported, so it stays backward compatible.
handoff: Wiring needed for robots and path limits. (1) crawl.ts owner: add `robots: RobotsPolicy` to AuditCrawlResult and return the policy fetched at crawl.ts:226 (`robots`). (2) analyse-site.ts owner: add `robots?: CheckLinksOptions['robots']` and `pathLimits?: CheckLinksOptions['pathLimits']` to AnalysisInput and forward both into the checkLinks call (analyse-site.ts:137-147). (3) BE-192 in pipeline.ts stages.analyseSite({...}) around lines 368-379: pass `robots: crawl.robots` and `pathLimits: { includePaths: deps.request.limits.includePaths, excludePaths: deps.request.limits.excludePaths, startPath: new URL(deps.request.url).pathname }`. Use the request URL's pathname, the same value the crawl gives pathLimitVerdict (crawl.ts:220); do not use the pipeline's local startPath from startPathOf(), which is the landed page's path and query. The checkout/payment refusal needs no wiring.
